task.name: Backfill historical URL-backed product media into managed media identities

head_policy.description: For an active branch task, the live task/PR head may differ from task_head only by descendant commits whose complete diff from task_head is restricted to the canonical execution-state file. Completed merged tasks retain their accepted code task_head plus explicit merge evidence.

acceptance_criteria: Inventory every historical product_images row still using legacy URL authority (including source=legacy_url and/or missing managed media identity as defined by the current schema) and produce a deterministic tenant-aware unresolved set before mutation.

Perform only additive reconciliation/backfill: where authoritative tenant ownership and storage/binary provenance can be proven, create or reuse the correct managed media asset and link the historical product image through media_asset_id with source=managed without deleting the legacy URL during P2-D.

Do not convert an untrusted arbitrary historical delivery URL into managed identity by blind network fetching or assumption; rows whose ownership, storage source or binary cannot be proven remain explicitly unresolved and must fail the zero-unresolved acceptance gate.
Preserve product/vendor tenant ownership and prevent cross-vendor media association throughout discovery, reconciliation and verification.

Preserve file existence, content hash or equivalent integrity metadata where available, MIME/size metadata where available, sort_order, alt text, primary/first-image semantics and current read parity when a legacy row becomes managed.

Make the backfill deterministic and safe to retry: already reconciled rows must not duplicate media assets or change semantic identity, and interrupted execution must be recoverable/forward-fix without double-application.
Prove behavior and data parity across the repository-supported SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL paths, including representative legacy, already-managed, unresolved and cross-tenant fixtures.

Require zero unresolved historical legacy product-media rows before any future compatibility fallback or legacy URL storage removal may even be proposed; P2-D itself must not remove the dual-read fallback, legacy URL column/storage or older-client compatibility.

Keep P2-D limited to historical product-media additive backfill, verification and the smallest necessary migration/data tooling/tests; no unrelated Admin/storefront redesign, customer media-library scope, dependency/config/RBAC expansion or destructive cleanup.

Exact final implementation head must be current with protected main, have no unresolved review blocker, and pass Governance, CodeQL and full CI including static/build, SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, browser E2E/WCAG/W3C and runtime integration/restore/launch before merge.

architecture_decisions.decision: Treat canonical-state-only descendant commits as code-equivalent to task_head for head reconciliation and hosted acceptance evidence.
architecture_decisions.reason: A commit cannot embed its own final SHA inside the state file it contains; without this rule every canonical-state update would invalidate itself.

architecture_decisions.decision: VSN Commerce original project materials are proprietary / closed-source; project metadata must not grant GPLv3 or another open-source project license without a new explicit owner decision.
architecture_decisions.reason: Repository owner explicitly rejected GPLv3 on 2026-08-28; ADR-0001 records the decision while preserving third-party licenses.

architecture_decisions.decision: Remove residual client-side/static authority in small domain batches before retiring the global StoreProvider or redesigning Admin.
architecture_decisions.reason: Current Laravel mode is mandatory, but residual unreachable legacy branches still create dual-authority regression risk; consumer-first removal is safer than a giant deletion.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use Product.jsx as the second P1 consumer-first batch before Systems.jsx and global StoreProvider retirement.
architecture_decisions.reason: Product.jsx directly imported the static catalog and global store and contained multiple apiBackend branches; P1-B removed that consumer-side legacy authority while preserving Laravel contracts.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use Systems.jsx as the third P1 consumer-first batch and migrate its customer-system domains incrementally before global StoreProvider retirement.
architecture_decisions.reason: P1-C removed Systems live-route apiBackend/useStore/static-catalog authority while preserving the named route surface and server-authoritative customer/system contracts.

architecture_decisions.decision: Make the final P1 batch verification-first: prove residual StoreProvider/useStore/static-catalog consumers before global legacy client-state retirement.
architecture_decisions.reason: The final P1 implementation proved all downstream consumers were migrated before unmounting StoreProvider and deleting the legacy store/catalog authority, with a retained source walker preventing regression.

architecture_decisions.decision: Begin P2 with reconciliation of existing media contracts rather than immediate rewrites.
architecture_decisions.reason: Product managed-media writes and seller-logo stable media ID behavior already have semantic coverage in the repository. P2 should preserve correct work, identify only real lifecycle/reference/legacy-data gaps, and avoid duplicating existing services or migrations.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use the existing backend stable seller-logo ID contract and remove SellerSettings' URL-as-selection-identity seam before broader remaining-image-field or historical-media work.
architecture_decisions.reason: Protected main already validates and persists logoMediaAssetId, resolves presentation URLs, enforces seller/global scope and now protects active storefront references from archive. SellerSettings still submitted MediaLibraryPanel item.url, making direct ID-native frontend/API completion the smallest remaining proven gap without schema churn.

architecture_decisions.decision: Classify remaining media/file/URL surfaces by domain semantics before attempting any further normalization; do not force domain-scoped files, provider URLs, navigation URLs or dormant fields into the reusable media library by naming similarity alone.
architecture_decisions.reason: Post-P2-B protected-main audit found no new active arbitrary first-party image URL writer: review images use uploaded disk/path storage with derived URLs, message attachments use immutable disk/path records, KYC uses private document paths, shipping labels are provider URLs, categories/promotions/games introduce no separate image URL writer, and avatar_path is exposed but has no current profile write contract. The only known historical URL-backed first-party media authority remains product legacy data, which is reserved for P2-D additive backfill.

architecture_decisions.decision: Perform historical product-media transition as additive, evidence-driven reconciliation only; preserve the legacy URL fallback/storage until zero unresolved rows and independent later authorization permit compatibility cleanup.
architecture_decisions.reason: Accepted P2-A evidence established nullable media_asset_id plus legacy_url source as the intentional dual-generation transition seam. Ownership/storage provenance, file integrity, metadata/order/alt/read parity and tenant isolation must be proven before stable managed identity is linked; destructive cleanup is explicitly outside P2-D.

known_risks: AGENTS.md still contains stale P0/P1 status text and 2026-08-22 media findings; repository evidence and this canonical checkpoint supersede historical status labels until the plan document is reconciled.

Historical URL-backed product/media rows are now the active P2-D data-migration risk: some rows may lack provable tenant ownership, recoverable storage provenance, binary existence or sufficient integrity metadata and must remain explicit unresolved blockers rather than being guessed into managed identity.
Blind remote fetching of historical URLs would convert delivery-location data into untrusted ingestion authority and is not authorized by the accepted additive migration strategy.
Backfill must be idempotent and must not duplicate media assets, cross vendor boundaries, reorder product media, lose alt text or silently change first-image/read semantics.

The dual-read legacy URL fallback and legacy URL storage must remain until a later independently authorized compatibility-removal task follows mechanically proven zero-unresolved evidence; P2-D is not destructive cleanup.
user_profiles.avatar_path remains a dormant/read-only legacy-shaped field; P2-D is product-media historical backfill only and must not expand into speculative customer media-library scope.
Domain-scoped review images, message attachments and KYC documents plus provider/navigation URLs remain outside P2-D reusable media migration scope under the accepted P2-C classification.
The backend seller logoUrl compatibility resolver may still serve older clients/data and must not be removed by P2-D unless independent later evidence and authorization explicitly cover it.
Third-party dependencies retain their own license obligations even though the project-level VSN Commerce materials are proprietary.

AGENTS.md and some README progress prose remain stale relative to verified repository state and should be reconciled without rewriting historical audit context.
